Honeyed Porridge

Served at: Imbolc Day Celebration

Serves 2Prep 5 minCook 10-15 min

Honeyed Porridge is a simple, comforting dish traditionally enjoyed during Imbolc, a Celtic festival celebrating the first signs of spring and the return of light. This warm, nourishing meal symbolizes sustenance and the sweetness of new beginnings, offering a gentle start to a day of reflection and hope as winter begins to wane.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (90 g) rolled oats (not instant)
  • 2 cups (470 ml) milk (dairy or non-dairy)
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) water
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 2-4 tablespoons honey, plus more for serving
  • Optional toppings: fresh fruit, chopped nuts, cinnamon

Method

  1. Combine the rolled oats, milk, water, and salt in a medium saucepan.
  2. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
  3. Reduce the heat to low and continue to cook, stirring frequently, for 5-10 minutes, or until the oats are tender and the porridge has thickened to your desired consistency.
  4. Remove the saucepan from the heat and stir in 2-4 tablespoons of honey, adjusting to your taste preference.
  5. Ladle the warm porridge into bowls.
  6. Serve immediately, drizzling with additional honey and adding any desired toppings like fresh fruit, chopped nuts, or a sprinkle of cinnamon.

Tips

  • For a creamier porridge, use all milk instead of a milk and water combination.
  • Adjust the cooking time and liquid amount to achieve your preferred porridge consistency; some prefer it thicker, others thinner.
  • Experiment with different spices like a pinch of nutmeg or cardamom for an extra layer of warmth and flavor.
